bugs.title: Ad player swap unmutes a user who had muted (ignores the last mute decision)
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: The SSAI ad path covers Twitch with a separate clean hls.js frame that is started muted (Chrome autoplay). revealOverlay() then sent mute:false unconditionally. The native mute was captured (wasMuted/holdWasMuted) but only used to restore the native player at ad-end, so every pod handed sound back to a user who had muted. Two more paths broke the same decision: a warm standby minted at page load carried the mute state from load time (stale after a later mute), and the document-wide pointerdown handler unmuted on any click, including a click in chat. ad-end also restored wasMuted instead of the decision the user made during the pod (an explicit badge unmute was lost).
bugs.falsifier: On a real Twitch live with a user-muted native player, the clean ad frame starts playing audio, or a click outside the badge restores audio, or the native player comes back unmuted/muted against the user's last decision.
evidence: Owner report 2026-10-26: 'when i mute, the ad comes, player swaps, it unmutes. respect the last user decision.'

Pre-fix code, kick-overlay/twitch-adblock.js revealOverlay(): `if (!overlay.unmuteTried) { overlay.unmuteTried = true; overlaySend({ t: 'mute', m: false }); ... }` with no read of wasMuted/holdWasMuted
Pre-fix code, stopAdOverlay(): `v.muted = overlay.wasMuted` — captured at pod start, so an in-pod unmute was reverted
Pre-fix code, unmuteHandler on document pointerdown: unmuted on ANY page click, regardless of the user's mute

kick-overlay/mute-decision-test.cjs runs the real twitch-adblock.js through ad-hold -> ad-start -> frame ready -> 3 healthy Playing ticks -> reveal in a stubbed DOM: muted user gets no mute:false (and the badge offers click-to-sound), a generic page click does not unmute, a badge click does, ad-end restores the decision; an unmuted user still gets sound
Its negative arm replays the pre-fix gate (`if (overlay.muteIntent)` -> `if (false)`) and the muted scenario then DOES see mute:false, so the detector is exercised in both directions
Gate: node _tools/ko-verify.mjs -> RESULT PASS checks=12 failed=0, including the new mute-decision check
bugs.next: Owner: mute the stream, wait for an ad pod (or reload a channel with a preroll), then confirm the clean player stays silent, the badge says 'clique para som', and the native player comes back in the same mute state. NOT MEASURED: the real pod in the owner's Chrome.

bugs.title: Black box over a YouTube watch page with player=kick (fixed in 0.8.42: `ready` was posted to the hardcoded twitch.tv origin)
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: player-bridge.js posts `ready` to PARENT_ORIGIN, which is `https://www.twitch.tv` until a valid inbound message teaches the frame the real parent origin. On a youtube.com page the browser silently drops that post (targetOrigin mismatch), so the content script never sees `ready`, never hands over the pending playback_url, and the IVS player stays Idle until the 15s never-played watchdog tears the layer down. The origin is only learned when a kickSend lands AFTER the frame's load event (mute/volume/play from a later show), and `ready` is never re-posted, so the frame stays half-initialised for its whole life.
bugs.falsifier: CORRECTED by measurement (0.8.41). The pre-instrumentation falsifier ('KO.kickReady becomes true and the layer plays') is what the fix must satisfy; the measured falsifier for THIS cause is: a frame->page post with targetOrigin https://www.twitch.tv is actually delivered on a youtube.com page, or the frame reports `ready` accepted by the content script while `parentLearnedAt` is still 0.
evidence: Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jfKfPfyJRdk, ko.v2 player=kick, mapping rodil -> {kick: rodil, yt: that video}
Guest Chrome 2026-10-26 (0.8.41 instrumentation), frame token d20935ab matched on BOTH sides (page KO.kickFrame.dataset.koToken === frame __koBridgeDiag.token)
Frame side, before any inbound message: posts.ready=1 at ms=684 with to='https://www.twitch.tv', learned=false; posts.st=7 also to twitch.tv; parentLearnedAt=0; inbound.total=0
Page side, same moment: KO.kickDiag.accepted=0, drops={} (nothing was dropped by the page guards), KO.kickReady=false, KO.pendingUrl=true

Primitive check, same frame: frame->page postMessage with targetOrigin 'https://www.twitch.tv' delivered 0 times (parent is youtube.com); page->frame with '*' delivered, and with the extension origin delivered

Causal arm: one valid inbound getState from the page -> frame parentLearnedAt=8432ms, learnedFrom={origin:'https://www.youtube.com', fromParent:true}, inbound={total:1,accepted:1}; the page then accepts st immediately (accepted 0 -> 2, byType {st:2}, firstAt.st=9393). ready is still never accepted (readyFrame=null): it was posted once, at 684ms, before the origin was known

Explains the earlier run in this ticket: st only started arriving at 21.4s, right after the first successful kickSend (mute/volume/play at 21.2s, sentByType {mute,volume,play}); before that showKickLayer's sends were blocked (KO.kickDiag.blockedSend=4) because KO.kickWin is only set on the frame's load event
Teardown branch unchanged: the 15s never-played watchdog fires because kickEverPlayed stays false and kickState stays Idle

Fix 0.8.42, measured on a real youtube.com parent: the extension's own player.html iframe, created from the page the way content.js does it, delivered `ready` to the page at ms=108 BEFORE any inbound message; the frame reported firstPost.ready={ms:104,to:'*',learned:false}. After one valid getState the frame reports learned=true, learnedFrom={origin:'https://www.youtube.com',fromParent:true} at 2779ms and keeps posting

Fix 0.8.42, unit arm: kick-overlay/bridge-handshake-test.cjs runs the real player-bridge.js against a parent that enforces targetOrigin like the browser (wrong origin = dropped, never delivered). 18 checks; its negative arm restores the pre-fix default and MUST see the drop, which it does. Gate check `bridge-handshake`

NOT re-measured: the full overlay mount on a YouTube watch page. The mapped kick channel rodil reports livestream.is_live=false right now, so the page never fetched a playback url (KO.activeUrl empty, KO.kickUrlT 0) and no layer mounted. External condition, unrelated to this fix
bugs.owner_validation: not requested: needs a mapped channel whose kick side is live
bugs.next: Owner: on a mapped channel whose kick side is live, open the YouTube watch page with ko.v2 player=kick and confirm the layer plays (kickReady=true, state Playing) instead of a black box. The guest-side falsifier is closed; the owner sample is still missing.

bugs.title: Overlay pinned over a channel sub-route (clips/videos) after SPA navigation
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: Twitch keeps its .persistent-player element (and the <video> inside it) in the DOM after an SPA navigation to /<channel>/clips, /videos or /about. rectTick() mirrored that ghost rect, so the position:fixed layer stayed on top of the new layout instead of disappearing. Hosts also port the clip viewer and hover previews outside main, so 'largest visible video' could pick the wrong player on a channel page.
bugs.falsifier: On /<channel>/clips (and /videos) the wrap is still display:block with a non-zero rect, or the overlay mounts there on a fresh load.
evidence: Guest Chrome, before the fix, SPA channel -> /rodil/clips: #ko-wrap display:block, left 730.5 top 142.1 w 533 h 299.8 over the clips grid (screenshot G:/Temp/opencode/ko-clips-1600.png)
Guest Chrome, before the fix, SPA channel -> /rodil/videos: same pinned rect over the video grid (G:/Temp/opencode/ko-videos-now.png)
Guest Chrome, after the fix, same SPA to /rodil/clips and /rodil/videos: #ko-wrap removed (null), native <video> resumed (paused:false)
Guest Chrome, after the fix, back to /rodil: wrap re-mounted, ko-placed, rect 714x325 over the player (G:/Temp/opencode/ko-back-root.png)
kick-overlay/route-gate-test.cjs PASS: route contract, immediate hide on route change, no mount on a non-player route, no paint from an unplaced wrap
bugs.next: Owner: open a mapped channel, click the Clips tab, then Videos, then back to the channel. The overlay must be gone on both sub-pages and reappear over the player on the channel root.

bugs.title: Cold preroll native ad stays visible too long
bugs.author: lane
bugs.hypothesis: Early prewarm plus a fast standby handoff shrinks the window in which the native ad is visible on a cold open.
bugs.falsifier: A real cold open still reveals the clean frame more than 2 s after ad-start.
evidence: Edge synthetic ad-hold + ad-start: reveal in 136-547 ms (2026-10-23)
Edge real rodil: preroll at 3.3 s and 4.3 s beat the 2.6 s and 3.3 s fast prewarm; rebuilt and revealed at 6.8 s and 7.8 s
Edge offline duda: no standby and no retry loop
bugs.next: Owner F5 a real cold open on 0.8.32. If the reveal is still over 2 s, try a cached clean URL or an earlier worker start.
